clue.text: Humorous, it comes to screen — the full-length version?

definitions.text: Humorous, it comes to screen — the full-length version?

parts.note: surface reading: a funny programme that gets broadcast on television
setter's reading: the usual short name for such a show is a clipped form, and this asks for its two words written out in full

explanation.surface: Someone describes a comedy coming to the screen and wonders whether it is the uncut, full-length edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full-length version' sounds like a director's cut, but it means the unabbreviated name: the show is usually called a sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television series of humorous episodes built around recurring characters, usually shortened to sitcom.

clue.text: Little time in hunt for blandishments

indicators.note: in places the small pieces inside the verb for pursuing prey that follows

parts.note: to stalk prey is to hunt it
wee is Scottish and informal British for small
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A hunter uses a little time to coax the quarry with flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet talk is flattering, persuasive speech, which is what blandishments are.

clue.text: Flier's rôle, swinging up with lack of effort, say?

definitions.text: Flier's rôle, swinging up with lack of effort, say?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

indicators.note: say asks for a word that matches the sound of the phrase before it, not its spelling

parts.note: ease is a lack of effort; the letters given are pronounced the same way

explanation.surface: A circus flier swings upwards effortlessly in the role of an acrobat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the high flier swinging up with apparent ease on this circus bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is the swinging bar on which an aerial acrobat, the flier, performs.

clue.text: Fossil, a little one with day inscribed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something inscribed is written into a surface, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a mite is a small child or tiny creature
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A small fossil bears a date carved into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammonite is the coiled shell fossil of an extinct marine mollusc.

clue.text: Page within a page, it's entangled?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an extra leaf or small panel placed inside a larger page
second meaning, split in two: something entangled is caught in a set, a snare or net

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical, hence the question mark: read the answer as two words, 'in set', describing something caught up in a trap or tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a smaller page, map or picture placed inside a larger one in a publication.

clue.text: Danseur: I'm remarkably tender

indicators.note: remarkably suggests these letters are behaving in an unusual way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A male ballet dancer boasts that he is unusually gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective about the dancer, but it is a noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is employed to look after, or tend, young children, so she is a tender of them.

clue.text: Sage or coriander originally in brew

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the drink named after it

parts.note: ale is a brewed beer

indicators.note: originally points to how the word starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of coriander

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether to flavour a beer with sage or coriander.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage looks like the herb beside coriander, but it is the definition, meaning a wise person.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person regarded as an infallible source of wise counsel, as a sage is.

clue.text: Land, not sea, I gathered

indicators.note: things gathered together are bundled up and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that what they see is land rather than sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a country, and a country is a land; it borders the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Line going up, boundary always vertical

indicators.note: in a down entry, vertical tells us the pieces stand upright and read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: in cricket a six is a boundary hit clearing the rope on the full
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A boundary line on a field always runs straight up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a hit that clears the boundary without bouncing scores six runs and is itself called a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The y-axis is the vertical line on a graph, running upward from the origin.

clue.text: Calculations appear to be switched for theologian and scholar

indicators.note: switched round here means the whole phrase is turned to read the opposite way

parts.note: sums are arithmetical calculations
are, taken as the verb of being

explanation.surface: The figures have been swapped around by a learned theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: Read SUMS ARE right to left. Erasmus was a Dutchman, one of the puzzle's theme of 11/12.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Renaissance humanist scholar and Catholic theologian.

clue.text: Payment to central government fund went on courses for the auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor here is a listener, so the words are to be judged by sound

parts.note: rode means went on horseback or by vehicle
tacks are the courses a sailing boat takes against the wind

explanation.surface: An auditor checks whether a government fund was spent on courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant inspecting payments; it means a listener. Road tax is the British vehicle excise duty paid to keep a car on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Road tax is a charge paid by vehicle owners into the government's revenue.

clue.text: What connects 9, 13, 15, 20 and 28, after which number comes down

parts.note: then means after that, next
a number is something that numbs; ether is an anaesthetic
an aircraft lands when it comes down

explanation.surface: A note explains a link between entries, after which a number appears in the down clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the crossword trick for an anaesthetic, something that makes you numb. The five referenced answers are all Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus, Tasman, Hals, Gullit and William of Orange are all Dutch, so their common link is their country.

clue.text: See 11
Isle found east of a geographical region, as explorer

indicators.note: in an across entry east is to the right, so the island follows the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a belt is a zone or region, as in the Corn Belt
taken as written
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An island is located to the east of a region, as an explorer would note.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was a seventeenth-century Dutch seafarer, famous as an explorer of the southern oceans.

clue.text: Short root, large amount that's often served with nachos

indicators.note: short means the word is cut and loses its final letter

parts.note: the root of something is its source
reams means a large quantity, especially of paper

explanation.surface: A cut-down root vegetable and a big helping are served with nachos.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour cream is a cultured dairy topping commonly served with nachos alongside salsa and guacamole.

clue.text: Artist applauds: I will be thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out means ejected, so that piece is removed from the word

parts.note: to hail someone is to acclaim them
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist cheers an audience, then declares they will be ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age portrait painter, known for The Laughing Cavalier.

clue.text: Triangular item assigned shape

parts.note: set means assigned, as a set task
a square is a shape

explanation.surface: A triangular object has been given a particular shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays a triangle against a square.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a flat right-angled triangle used for drawing lines and angles.

clue.text: Cheese turns me off, tiniest piece of Edam eaten …

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so this letter sits within the other piece
off suggests going wrong, as milk does, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the smallest piece of a word is a single letter, its first

parts.note: the first letter of Edam

explanation.surface: A cheese puts someone off, though a tiny crumb of Edam has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads on to the next clue, which also involves cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Muenster is a mild semi-soft cheese, an American spelling of the French Munster.

clue.text: Eccentric, however you look at it

indicators.note: if it looks the same from either side, the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: describes a word that reads identically either way

explanation.surface: Someone is declared an oddball, whichever way you view them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is followed only by a description of the answer's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Kook is American slang for a strange or crazy person, an eccentric.

clue.text: … where cheese may be cooking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: placed in a bread roll, as in a sandwich
second meaning: going well, enjoying a run of success

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like melting cheese in a kitchen, but it is slang for doing well, as in 'now we're cooking'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a roll means enjoying a streak of success; literally, cheese sits on a roll in a sandwich.

clue.text: Reportedly offensive winger, Italian footballer

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: rude means offensive
a gull is a winged seabird
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: An Italian footballer on the wing is said to be an attacking player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive winger' looks like an attacking wide player; it splits into rude and a bird. Ruud Gullit is the Dutch footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruud Gullit is a Dutch former footballer who captained the Netherlands and later played in Italy for AC Milan.

clue.text: Force blockading British country

indicators.note: to blockade is to surround and seal off, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to lean on someone is to pressure or force them
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A military force blockades a British territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a country on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Greek character lies about item on breakfast menu?

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around and moved, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A Greek man tells untruths about what is offered at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit, typically eaten for breakfast.

clue.text: What 9, 13, 15, 20 or 28 might say that's highly unlikely!

definitions.text: What 9, 13, 15, 20 or 28 might say that's highly unlikely!

parts.note: literal reading: a statement of nationality these five men could truthfully make
setter's reading: an old British phrase tacked onto an absurd claim to show disbelief

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'If that's true, then I'm a Dutchman' dismisses something as impossible; from the five Dutch themed men it would simply be true.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses complete disbelief, while for these Netherlanders it is a plain statement of fact.

clue.text: Relative where one finds Hollywood wife

parts.note: Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A relative explains where a Hollywood wife is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollywood wife' looks like one phrase but splits: where Hollywood is, then the wife's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent or sibling.

clue.text: Legal requirement with 10 providing theme

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test British cars must pass, a legal requirement alongside road tax
providing means on condition that, if

explanation.surface: A legal requirement, along with a tax, supplies a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the MOT is the compulsory yearly vehicle test, named after the old Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or element in a work, which is a theme.

clue.text: King and Queen feast outside?

parts.note: B.B. King was the American blues guitarist
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: A king and queen hold a banquet in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' gives the initials of the blues musician B.B. King, not the usual K or R.
explanation.definitionFit: BBQ is the abbreviation for barbecue, a meal cooked and eaten outdoors, hence a feast outside.

clue.text: First of errors by steeplejack's ending in inaccurate inspection

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the adjective that follows

parts.note: a loose translation is an inaccurate one

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of steeplejack

indicators.note: ending points to the last letter of the possessive word before it

parts.note: the first letter of errors

explanation.surface: A steeplejack's sloppy survey of a spire leads to the first errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here means beside: the letter from errors is placed after everything else, not inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal word for a quick look or inspection.

clue.text: Blockbuster film cut a magical character

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the film's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Titanic, the 1997 James Cameron blockbuster
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blockbuster film has a magical character edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' sounds like film editing; it trims the last letter of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, a figure of magic.

clue.text: Nation's father is bound to go far with one aim for reform

parts.note: will expresses what is bound to happen

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A national founder is destined to succeed, driven by a single goal of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Orange, also called William the Silent, led the Dutch revolt against Spain and is honoured as the Father of the Fatherland.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Orange is known in the Netherlands as Vader des Vaderlands, the father of the Dutch nation.
